title: fix(a11y): set aria-pressed on CollectionButton in page-grid-selector
author: app/claude
body:
## Summary

`PageButton` and `PageListItem` already expose their selection state via `aria-pressed={isActive}`, but `CollectionButton` in the same file did not, so screen reader users could not tell which collection was currently selected. This change mirrors the existing pattern by passing the `isActive` prop through to `aria-pressed` on the collection button element.

## WCAG

- **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** (Level AA): selected/pressed state must be programmatically determinable.

## Changes

- `web/src/components/page-grid-selector.tsx` — add `aria-pressed={isActive}` to the `CollectionButton`'s `<button>` (mirrors `PageButton` at ~line 213 and `PageListItem` at ~line 303).
- `web/src/__tests__/page-grid-selector.test.tsx` — add a test that renders two collections with one active and asserts `aria-pressed="true"` on the selected one and `aria-pressed="false"` on the other.

No new user-facing strings were added, so no `next-intl` keys needed updates.

## Confidence and what to double-check

- **High confidence** that the attribute is correctly set: `isActive` is already threaded into the component (used to style the active card border and indicator), so there is no new derivation logic — just exposing it to assistive tech.
- I was **unable to run `npm test` locally** in this sandbox (no docker-compose access). CI will run the test, and `web/tests/a11y.spec.ts` should stay green since this only adds an attribute. Please verify the test run in CI before merging.
- Visual styling is unchanged. A reviewer may want to spot-check the Collections tab in the dev container to confirm nothing visual shifted — but `aria-pressed` does not trigger any CSS in this codebase (active state is class-based via `isActive`), so this should be a no-op visually.

Closes #1200

reviews.author: github-actions[bot]
reviews.body:
**No a11y concerns — clean fix.**

This change adds `aria-pressed={isActive}` to `CollectionButton`, bringing it in line with `PageButton` and `PageListItem` which already carried the same attribute. A few quick checks:

- **Accessible name** — the button's name comes from the visible `{collection.name}` text, so no `aria-label` gap. The `GalleryHorizontalEnd` icon is decorative and doesn't need `aria-hidden` here (the text label is sufficient). ✅
- **`aria-pressed` type** — `isActive: boolean` so React emits `aria-pressed="true"` / `aria-pressed="false"` correctly (WCAG 4.1.2). ✅
- **Consistency** — matches the existing pattern on the sibling button components in the same file. ✅
- **No hardcoded strings** — no new user-facing literals; the loading skeleton's `aria-label` already uses a `next-intl` key (`t("loadingPreviewsAriaLabel")`). ✅
- **Test** — the added test asserts both the `true` and `false` states, which is the right shape for a toggle-button contract. ✅

One low-priority note (not a blocker): `aria-pressed` models a toggle (on/off); `aria-current="true"` or a `role="option"` + `aria-selected` inside a listbox would be a slightly closer semantic match for "the currently displayed collection". The existing codebase already uses `aria-pressed` for this pattern across all three button types, so changing it is out of scope here — just worth revisiting if the component is refactored.

title: fix(a11y): page-builder — label export dialog textarea
author: app/claude
body:
## Summary

The share-string `<textarea>` in the page-builder export dialog had no programmatic label. Screen-reader users focusing the field heard only "edit text, read only" with no indication of what it contains.

Adds `aria-label={t("exportStringAriaLabel")}` routed through `next-intl`, so the field announces as "Share string" (translated per locale).

**WCAG criteria:**
- 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A) — form controls must have programmatically associated labels
- 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level AA) — all form inputs must have an accessible name

## Changes

- `web/src/components/page-builder.tsx` — add `aria-label` to the textarea at the location flagged in the issue (~line 1540)
- `web/messages/{en,de,es,fr,it,ja,ko,nl,pl,pt,ru,sv,tr,zh}.json` — add `pageBuilder.exportStringAriaLabel` key in all 14 locales
- `web/tests/regression/pages-edit.spec.ts` — update the existing `pages.edit.export-dialog` test to locate the textarea by accessible name (`getByRole("textbox", { name: "Share string" })`) instead of a bare CSS selector. This is the test that would have caught the bug and now guards against regression.

## Confidence

- **High** — change is local, follows the issue's "Option 1" exactly, and mirrors the existing `exportCopyAriaLabel` translation pattern already used for the copy button in the same dialog.
- **Translations were authored from the existing in-locale phrasing of `exportCopyAriaLabel`** (e.g. de "Freigabezeichenfolge kopieren" → "Freigabezeichenfolge"). A native-speaker review would be nice-to-have but the strings are nominal nouns lifted from existing translations, so risk is low.

## What I tested

- All 14 locale JSON files re-parse cleanly with the new key present (verified with `python3 json.load`).
- Visually inspected the JSX change in context.

## What I could not test locally

- I did not run `web/tests/a11y.spec.ts` or the regression suite — the dev container wasn't running in this sandbox and per `CLAUDE.md` web tests must run inside Docker. CI will exercise both. The updated `pages.edit.export-dialog` test asserts on `name: "Share string"` (English), which matches the default locale used by the test suite.

## What a reviewer should double-check

- Native-speaker sanity on the 13 non-English translations (all derived from the corresponding `exportCopyAriaLabel` translation).
- Confirm `a11y.spec.ts` and `pages-edit.spec.ts` both pass in CI.

Closes #1195

title: fix(a11y): use <Link> for /schedule navigation in ActivePageDisplay
author: app/claude
body:
## Summary

Two affordances in `web/src/components/active-page-display.tsx` navigated to `/schedule` via `<button onClick={() => router.push("/schedule")}>`. Screen readers heard "button" (in-page action), which is the wrong semantic for a navigation control.

Closes #1197

## What changed

- Replace both `<button>` elements with `<Link href="/schedule">` from `@/components/smart-link` (the existing app-wide anchor wrapper used in other components).
- Drop the now-unused `useRouter` import + call in this component.
- The remaining `<button>` elements in this file (Change Page, override-cancel ×, change-mode dialog options) are real in-page actions and stay as buttons.

## WCAG

- 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) — Level AA
- Assistive technology convention: `<button>` = action, `<a href>` = navigation

## Tests

- `web/src/__tests__/active-page-display.test.tsx`
  - The old "View Schedule" test asserted `getByRole("button", { name: /View Schedule/i })` and that `mockPush` was called with `/schedule`. Replaced with two regression tests that:
    1. assert `getByRole("link", { name: /View Schedule/i })` exists with `href="/schedule"`,
    2. assert the schedule-gap "Schedule settings" affordance is also a link with the same href,
    3. and that neither appears with `role="button"`.
- Added a `vi.mock("@/components/smart-link", ...)` stub to the three sibling test files that import `ActivePageDisplay` (`active-page-display-override`, `active-page-display-silence`, `live-output-home-sync`) so the component renders without a Router context. The mock mirrors the pattern already used in `pages-index-device-tabs.test.tsx`.
- Full web suite passes locally: `87 files, 1066 tests passed, 13 skipped`.

## Confidence / for human reviewer

- High confidence on the swap itself — `smart-link` already routes through `react-router`'s `Link`, so `useRouter().push("/schedule")` and `<Link href="/schedule">` produce identical client-side navigation.
- Visual styling is unchanged (same `className` strings on the new `<Link>`s), but a maintainer should double-check the underline + focus ring in the header-row "View Schedule →" against the live UI, since `<a>` has subtle default styling differences from `<button>` in some browsers.
- I did **not** run `tests/a11y.spec.ts` (Playwright) since this environment can't bring up the dev container. The change is strictly a role/semantics improvement, so I do not expect it to regress that suite.
- Pre-existing lint warnings in this file (`startTransition` before declaration, `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, missing `t` deps, i18next literal-string false positives for `→` and `.`) are unchanged.

reviews.author: github-actions[bot]
reviews.body:
**No a11y blockers — this PR is a net a11y improvement.**

## Summary

Both changes convert navigation-only `<button>` elements to proper `<a href>` links via `SmartLink`. This is the correct fix: screen reader users hear "link" (navigate away) rather than "button" (in-page action), and the elements now participate in standard browser navigation (open in new tab, copy link, etc.). WCAG 2.4.4 (Link Purpose) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) are both served.

---

## Findings

### Semantics fixed — `<button>` → `<Link href>` (WCAG 4.1.2 / 2.4.4)

`web/src/components/active-page-display.tsx` lines 372 & 476

Both `<button onClick={() => router.push(…)}>` affordances that navigate to `/schedule` are replaced with `<Link href="/schedule">`. `SmartLink` renders as a React Router `<Link>` for internal paths, which produces a proper `<a href>` in the DOM. Role, keyboard activation (Enter), right-click / middle-click, and URL exposure to AT all work correctly.

### Focus styles preserved

Both links carry over `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring rounded` — the existing visible-focus convention. No regression on WCAG 2.4.11.

### i18n keys confirmed

`t("viewSchedule")` → `"View Schedule"` and `t("scheduleSettingsLink")` → `"Schedule settings"` both exist in `web/messages/en.json` at the PR head. No hardcoded English labels introduced.

### Accessible names adequate (WCAG 4.1.2)

"View Schedule" and "Schedule settings" are unambiguous link labels that describe their destination. WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose satisfied.

### Tests enforce the semantic contract

New regression tests assert `getByRole("link")` (not `"button"`) and verify the `href` attribute — good guard against future regressions.

---

## Minor note (not a WCAG violation)

`web/src/components/active-page-display.tsx` line 374: the `→` arrow is appended as a hardcoded JSX character outside the i18n key — `{t("viewSchedule")} →`. Some screen readers will announce it as "right-pointing arrow"; others skip it. The label "View Schedule" remains clear regardless, so this is not a WCAG issue. It is a pre-existing pattern and out of scope for this PR.
